newsitem.title: UK: British water firms move to drought compensation.
newsitem.headline: British water firms move to drought compensation.

text.p: Changes to licences entitling customers to compensation from water companies for cuts in domestic supplies forced by a drought have been put into effect, industry watchdog Ofwat said.
The changes, agreed voluntarily by the companies, allow for compensation of 10 stg for each day or part of a day that domestic supplies are cut off.
The licence amendments were made on April 19.
Previous agreements had exempted companies from paying compensation if drought orders were obtained.
Four water and sewerage companies -- North West Water, part of United Utilities, South West, Hyder's Welsh Water and Wessex Water -- have had the changes formalised in their licences.
Ofwat said Anglian, Northumbrian, Severn Trent, Thames and Yorkshire had decided to adopt the compensation plans, but declined to agree to amendments in their licences.
Only Southern Water of the large water and sewerage companies has held back, Ofwat said.
The proposals were published by Ofwat on January 13.
